key_inputs: Polls published before the silence: Ipsos 20-22 Oct (n=3,624, commissioned by the SNS list; weight 0.69), NSPM 25 Sep-5 Oct (n=1,050; 0.21), Faktor Plus 16-20 Sep (n=986; 0.10); weights by recency (half-life 14 days) and sample size
All shares in percent of valid votes (Ipsos puts 2.5 % assumed invalid ballots into its base)

Past final polls 2020-2024 against official results: the SNS list was under-polled in four of five elections (2023 on average by 6.5 points) and over-polled in 2022; 25 % of each pollster's pooled SNS error and 50 % of its main-opposition error are carried over
Minority lists under-measured by polls in 2022-2023: SVM x1.25, other minority lists x1.35
Seats: D'Hondt over 250, threshold 3 % of voters who voted, minority lists exempt with quotients +35 % (2022 law, Art. 128-140); the function reproduces the official 2023 allocation exactly
Ranges and probabilities from 20,000 simulated outcomes: SNS error SD 4.9 points (the leave-one-out error of this method on 2020-2024), student list 4.0, correlation -0.7

Turnout: Ipsos 64.7 % (its final turnout estimates missed by +1.4, +0.1, -2.4, +3.5 in 2020, 2022, 2023, Belgrade 2024; half of the mean +0.65 removed) and Faktor Plus 62 % (Sep); 80 % range = +-1.28 x 3.0 points

sources.used_for: Ipsos poll 20-22 Oct 2026 (n=3,624, commissioned by the SNS list): all 18 lists and turnout; the main input (weight 0.69)
NSPM poll 25 Sep-5 Oct 2026 (n=1,050), decided voters (weight 0.21)
past pollster error: Ipsos final estimates 2020, 2022, 2023 and Belgrade 2024
past pollster error: NSPM final estimates 2020, 2022, 2023 and Belgrade 2024
official 2023 parliamentary results by municipality and Belgrade 2024 results (seat-function test, past errors, municipal pattern)
seat rules: Art. 128 threshold 3 % of voters who voted, Art. 129 D'Hondt over 250, Art. 140 minority lists exempt with quotients +35 %

contamination: While pre-cut-off poll articles were being fetched, election-day page headlines appeared in the sidebars of two news sites (reports of high morning turnout, one turnout figure for 10:00). Nothing from them is used: the turnout estimate was fixed at 11:46 CET from the Ipsos and Faktor Plus estimates before this was known and was not changed afterwards; no vote shares were seen.
notes: The SNS list leads on the central estimate (47.5 % to 40.2 %) but sits on the edge of a majority alone (125 seats; 53 % chance of 126+). Whether SPS clears the threshold (about 55 % chance) moves the SNS seat count by about four. Minority lists are expected to win about 11 seats thanks to the exemption and the 35 % bonus. Past final polls missed the SNS list by up to 9 points, in both directions, so the ranges are wide. The Ipsos poll dominates the average because it is the only one taken in the last two weeks.
